problem:
Find the substitution that will decouple the following system of differential equations: 

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-3{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)-2{x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}
$$

activity_context.topic_title: Solving Homogeneous Systems of ODEs With Distinct Eigenvalues

feedback.problem: Let ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ be eigenvectors of a matrix $A.$ Find the decoupling matrix of the differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we construct the matrix $E$, whose columns are the eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, the decoupling matrix can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & ={E}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot (-3)}[\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
